name: es30-deferred-shading
title: Deferred shading: G-buffer (MRT) + 48 moving point lights
summary: A procedurally generated 3D scene (tiled floor, boxes, spheres, pillars, torus, 48 glowing light markers) is rasterized once into a G-buffer (RGBA8 albedo+specular, RGB10_A2 normal, RG8 shininess+emissive, DEPTH_COMPONENT24 texture) with glDrawBuffers; the lighting pass rebuilds world positions from the depth texture and accumulates 48 coloured moving point lights either in one full-screen pass or with additive light volumes (instanced spheres, ONE/ONE blending). G-buffer planes and depth are compared with ray-cast analytic values, final pixels with a CPU lighting model, and the whole image with a forward-rendered reference using per-pixel quantization budgets; four controls (one light disabled, blending off, normal plane overwritten, front-face culling off) prove the comparisons can fail.
spec: ES 3.0 §4.2.1 Selecting Buffers for Writing (glDrawBuffers, DRAW_BUFFERi); §3.9.2.3 Shader Outputs (fragment output locations, glGetFragDataLocation)

ES 3.0 §3.8.3.1 Required Texture Formats and Table 3.13 (RGBA8, RGB10_A2 and RG8 are colour-renderable, RGBA16F is texture-only), Table 3.14 (DEPTH_COMPONENT24); §3.8.4 glTexStorage2D; §3.8.13 Texture Completeness (a depth texture with TEXTURE_COMPARE_MODE NONE needs NEAREST filters)
ES 3.0 §4.4.2 Attaching Images to Framebuffer Objects, §4.4.4 Framebuffer Completeness, §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries (COMPONENT_TYPE, component sizes, a missing component reads 0)

ES 3.0 §4.3.1 Selecting Buffers for Reading, §4.3.2 Reading Pixels (RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE for normalized fixed-point surfaces); §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point (one of the two closest values)

ES 3.0 §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (glClearBufferfv with a draw buffer index), §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test, §4.1.7 Blending (blend arithmetic in floating point, results clamped to [0, 1]), §4.1.9 Dithering

ES 3.0 §3.6.1 Basic Polygon Rasterization (face culling, front-face winding), §2.9.3 Drawing Commands (glDrawElementsInstanced, gl_InstanceID), §2.12.6 Uniform Variables (GetUniformBlockIndex, GetActiveUniformBlockiv, GetUniformIndices, GetActiveUniformsiv), §2.12.6.4 Standard Uniform Block Layout (std140), §2.12.6.5 Uniform Buffer Object Bindings

GLSL ES 3.00 §4.3.8.2 Output Layout Qualifiers, §4.3.8.3 Uniform Block Layout Qualifiers, §4.3.9 Interpolation (flat integer varying), §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers (samplers are lowp unless declared), §7.1 / §7.2 Special Variables (gl_VertexID, gl_InstanceID, gl_FragCoord), §8.8 texelFetch

api.glGenTextures: six render-target textures; their contents are read back and compared with analytic values
api.glBindTexture: G-buffer planes on units 0-3, light buffer on unit 4; the lighting and composite passes sample them
api.glActiveTexture: texture units 0-4; wrong unit assignment would break the deferred image, which is compared with the forward reference
api.glTexStorage2D: RGBA8, RGB10_A2, RG8, DEPTH_COMPONENT24, RGB10_A2 x2 storage; attachment bit sizes read back (RGB10_A2 = 10/10/10/2, RG8 = 8/8/0/0, depth >= 24) and contents verified
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST min/mag filters through the typed glTexParameter overloads: required for the depth texture to be complete (ES 3.0 3.8.13), proven by correct depth values read through it
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER / READ_FRAMEBUFFER targets: planes read back from the G-buffer FBO, final images from the default framebuffer
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: three colour textures at COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..2 and a depth texture at DEPTH_ATTACHMENT; OBJECT_TYPE = TEXTURE, sizes and contents verified
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: depth renderbuffer of the forward reference; the forward image matches the deferred image on all pixels, which requires its depth test to work
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE for the G-buffer with mixed formats (RGBA8, RGB10_A2, RG8, depth texture)
api.glRenderbufferStorage: DEPTH_COMPONENT24 storage; forward image equals the deferred image pixel by pixel
api.glDrawBuffers: {COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, 1, 2, NONE} on the G-buffer FBO: DRAW_BUFFER0..3 read back, and all three planes hold the analytic albedo / normal / shininess at the probe pixels
api.glReadBuffer: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..2 of the G-buffer FBO select the plane read by glReadPixels
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE of the three G-buffer planes (including the RGB10_A2 normal) and of the default framebuffer compared with analytic and forward values
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: COMPONENT_TYPE = UNSIGNED_NORMALIZED (x3), RED/GREEN/BLUE/ALPHA_SIZE of each plane, depth attachment OBJECT_TYPE = TEXTURE and DEPTH_SIZE >= 24
api.glClear: COLOR|DEPTH of the G-buffer: a background pixel reads albedo (0,0,0,0) and depth 1.0 (0xFFFFFF)
api.glClearColor: zero clear value of all G-buffer planes (background pixel check)
api.glClearBufferfv: COLOR with drawbuffer 1 sets the normal plane to (0.5, 1, 0.5) at every probe while the albedo plane keeps its values (control c)
api.glViewport: full-target viewport of every pass; the 65536-pixel comparison covers every pixel
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST, CULL_FACE, BLEND: occlusion order, culled back faces and additive accumulation are observable (controls b and d)
api.glDisable: BLEND, DEPTH_TEST, CULL_FACE restored per pass; DITHER off so stored values are exact
api.glDepthFunc: LESS: probes see the analytic nearest surface in the G-buffer depth
api.glDepthMask: TRUE for the geometry passes: depth values written
api.glCullFace: BACK for the scene (CPU winding check) and FRONT for the light volumes; without FRONT each light is added twice (control d)
api.glFrontFace: CCW: every mesh is counter-clockwise from outside (CPU check), so all surfaces survive culling
api.glBlendFunc: ONE, ONE for the light volumes: volume image equals the full-screen image; without blending it does not (control b)
api.glBlendEquation: FUNC_ADD: sums the per-light contributions (same evidence as glBlendFunc)
api.glUseProgram: gbuffer, forward, full-screen lighting, light-volume and composite programs; each renders its pass correctly
api.glGetUniformLocation: material, matrix, camera and sampler uniforms located; their values are observed in the images
api.glUniform1i: sampler unit indices, mode, light count and checker flag
api.glUniform1f: specular, shininess, emissive, exposure, volume scale: observed in G-buffer values and in the lit image
api.glUniform2f: near/far and viewport size used by the depth reconstruction; rebuilt positions match the analytic hit points
api.glUniform3f: albedo colours, camera position and view-ray basis; observed in the G-buffer and the rebuilt positions
api.glUniformMatrix3fv: normal matrix; normals of rotated, non-uniformly scaled boxes match the analytic normals
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: model and view-projection matrices; depth and positions match the analytic ray hits
api.glGetUniformBlockIndex: the Lights block found in the lighting program
api.glUniformBlockBinding: Lights block of three programs bound to binding point 0; light positions and colours seen in the image
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER, ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER (recorded in the VAO), UNIFORM_BUFFER
api.glBufferData: mesh data (STATIC_DRAW) and the 2048-byte light block (DYNAMIC_DRAW)
api.glBufferSubData: the light block is rewritten every frame; a light whose colour is zeroed disappears from the image exactly as the CPU model predicts (control a)
api.glGenVertexArrays: mesh VAO and an attribute-less VAO for the full-screen triangle
api.glVertexAttribPointer: interleaved position + normal (stride 24); normals and positions match the analytic geometry
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLES x3 with gl_VertexID: the full-screen triangle of the lighting and composite passes
api.glDrawElements: indexed meshes (UNSIGNED_SHORT), 81 draws per pass; every pixel of the deferred and forward images agrees
api.glDrawElementsInstanced: one light volume instance per light with gl_InstanceID selecting the light: the volume image equals the full-screen image

visual_review.notes: 256x256 captures of gpu (radeonsi), llvmpipe and zink es-max viewed (es-min identical to es-max on gpu; llvmpipe and zink differ from radeonsi by at most 15/255 and about 2/255 on average, because the 10-bit light accumulation rounds differently). A dark navy gradient sky above a grey-blue checkerboard slab seen from about 30 degrees above, ten pillars on a ring, boxes and glossy spheres, a golden torus around a silver sphere in the middle and 48 small glowing coloured bulbs; magenta and orange pools of light on the right and front, cyan and green on the left, soft specular highlights on the spheres and streaks on the floor, no seams at light-volume edges, no holes or flicker artifacts, clean silhouettes. A 512x512 G-buffer mosaic (albedo | normals over depth | lit result), the material view and the rebuilt-position grid (a smooth 1-unit grid that bends over spheres and pillars) were viewed as well; the forward-reference capture looks identical to the deferred one. A 640x360 windowed capture under xvfb also looked right.
